findings.detail: DNS resolution runs in a short-lived killable subprocess. The caller waits only within the shared monotonic task budget, leaves time to terminate and reap the resolver, rejects late results, and does not create a TCP socket or send an HTTP request after DNS consumes the deadline. Both HTTP and HTTPS use the deadline-bound connection factory, including redirect targets. No address cache or persistent resolver worker is used; fresh address results and the existing all-address TCP fallback preserve stale-address recovery.

A 303 changes every non-HEAD method to GET, clears the body and Content-Type, Content-Length, and Transfer-Encoding headers; HEAD remains HEAD. Existing 301/302 POST-to-GET handling and 307/308 method/body preservation remain. Authorization is stripped on cross-origin redirects.
